summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her sixth cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well with no acute complications. Her methotrexate levels showed appropriate clearance, and she completed leucovorin rescue as planned. An X-ray of her right foot, performed due to ongoing neuropathic pain, was normal, and an MRI of the foot was planned for outpatient follow-up. She developed expected mild transaminitis and neutropenia, both monitored without intervention. Her headache was managed with acetaminophen and oxycodone. She remained stable throughout the admission, was discharged home with instructions to complete three days of oral leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate, and will resume mesalamine after leucovorin completion. She is scheduled for her next chemotherapy cycle in two weeks.
problems: Other malignant lymphomas, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
Unspecified hereditary and idiopathic peripheral neuropathy
Antineoplastic and immunosuppressive drugs causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
